🔐Signed, daily codes

Each centre's code is cryptographically signed and expires at midnight, so yesterday's code or a forged one won't work, and a code alone does nothing without a parent's own account.

🪪A real person, not a PIN

Scanning needs the parent's own signed-in account, and only their own enrolled children at that centre can be checked in.

👀Verified at the door

Photo (or initials), full name and relationship on the parent's screen, so your educator confirms the right adult at a glance.

🧾A record for every scan

Time-stamped with who did it, straight into attendance and your reports, with instant alerts to family and staff.

KiddieTracSafe Arrival

No child expected today goes unnoticed

If a child hasn’t been signed in by their usual drop-off time and nobody has reported an absence, KiddieTrac asks the parents. If they don’t answer, the room’s educators and the director are alerted, so someone calls.

  • Checks every scheduled child, every 5 minutes, and skips closed days
  • Parents can answer “Not attending today” in one tap
  • A live board of who still needs a call, and a record of every check
See how Safe Arrival works →
9:00Ava and Leo are expectedBoth are scheduled today. Neither is signed in yet.
9:15Parents asked: “Has Ava arrived?”Once, by app notification, email or text, as each parent chose.
9:17Ava’s mom: not attending today, unwellRecorded as an absence. Ava’s check closes by itself.
9:35No answer for Leo: staff alertedThe room’s educators and the director get an alert with the parents’ numbers.
9:41Closed: “On the way, arriving 10:15”Saved with the educator’s name and note.

FAQ

Questions, answered

Yes — CWELCC and provincial subsidy automation are native, not bolt-ons. Subsidy amounts are calculated per child, deducted from invoices automatically, and your submission reports come pre-formatted for Ontario. We're PIPEDA-aligned with data hosted in North America.

Most agencies are live within days. You can import children and staff from a spreadsheet, we migrate from your current system free, and a dedicated onboarding specialist walks you through every feature. No IT department required.

White label means a parent app under your brand name, logo, colours and custom domain — plus branded emails and reports. It's a first-class feature available on every plan, typically launched in as little as 14 days.

Families can pay by Interac e-Transfer, direct bank EFT, Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Google Pay or Apple Pay — processed through Zūm Rails, Stripe or Helcim. KiddieTrac supports true CAD and USD dual-currency billing and syncs with QuickBooks, Xero and Sage, and exports Sage 50 and CSV files.

Each centre shows a QR code that changes every day and is cryptographically signed, and only your staff can display it. Parents scan it with their own signed-in KiddieTrac app, so a code on its own does nothing: only children enrolled at that centre on that parent's family can be checked in. After each scan the parent's screen shows their photo (or initials), full name and relationship, so your educator can confirm the right adult at a glance, and every check-in is time-stamped with who did it and shared instantly with the other parent and the room's educators.

With Safe Arrival on, KiddieTrac checks every scheduled child every 5 minutes. If a child hasn’t been signed in by their usual drop-off time plus your grace period, and no absence was reported, the parents are asked once by app notification, email or text. If nobody answers, the room’s educators and the director are alerted and the Safe Arrival board shows who still needs a call. Every check is recorded. How Safe Arrival works.

Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, hosted in North America, backed up daily, and protected with two-factor authentication and granular role-based permissions. We're built PIPEDA-first.

Every customer gets a dedicated onboarding specialist and direct access to a real human support team that knows Canadian childcare — replying within one business day.

Free Resource

CWELCC Compliance Checklist — 2026

The 18-point CWELCC compliance checklist

Everything Ontario childcare operators need to stay audit-ready under the Canada-Wide Early Learning & Child Care program.

✅ Tip: tick each box as you confirm it. Re-run quarterly to stay inspection-ready.

🍁 Enrolment & Eligibility

Confirm each child's age category (infant, toddler, preschool) for the correct funding stream.
Verify eligibility and enrolment dates for the CWELCC base-fee reduction.
Keep a signed parent enrolment agreement on file for every child.
Track licensed capacity vs. actual enrolment for each room.

💰 Fees & Subsidy

Apply the correct CWELCC fee reduction to every eligible child.
Reconcile subsidy amounts against the current provincial rate table.
Maintain a transparent fee schedule (gross fee, reduction, net parent fee).
Document any fee changes with their effective dates.

✅ Attendance & Records

Record daily check-in/check-out times for every child.
Retain attendance and financial records for the required retention period.
Log staff-to-child ratios for each room throughout the day.

📊 Reporting & Submission

Prepare monthly/quarterly CWELCC funding reports.
Submit enrolment and attendance data by every ministry deadline.
Track allocation vs. actual spend of CWELCC funding.
Keep payroll & wage-enhancement (WEG) records aligned with funding.

🔒 Audit Readiness

Store all records securely with role-based access.
Run a quarterly self-audit against this checklist.
Keep digital backups of agreements, invoices and reports.

Let KiddieTrac automate all of this

CWELCC subsidy math, submission reports and audit-ready records — generated for you automatically.

This checklist is a general guide and not legal advice. Always confirm current requirements with your ministry and licensing authority.

Province by province

KiddieTrac is used by licensed centres, home child care agencies and independent providers. The parts that differ between provinces are built in as settings, not workarounds:

Learning frameworks. Link observations and report cards to Ontario’s How Does Learning Happen? and ELECT, the British Columbia Early Learning Framework, Alberta’s Flight, Quebec’s Accueillir la petite enfance, or your own.

Fee reductions and subsidies. Set up your province’s reduced parent fee or a family’s subsidy per child, and invoices deduct it automatically. Ontario programs get CWELCC handled end to end: see CWELCC billing.

Your data. KiddieTrac is hosted in North America with encryption, two-factor sign-in and a full audit log. If your organization needs data stored in Canada, talk to us before you sign up.

Ontario ratio rules

A countdown for every sleeping child under 24 months at the interval in your sleep policy, an alert to the room’s educators and then the director when a check is overdue, physician sleep-position directions on the child’s record, and a report for your inspector.

Log missing-child drills with the area, the scenario and the time to locate the child, and see when the next one is due every 3 months, next to your monthly fire drills. Educators report hazards; directors record what was done and tell current families by email and in the app.

Who hears what

Parents first, then the people in the room

👪 Families

  • Asked once, when the grace period after the expected time has passed.
  • The message goes through each parent’s own choices: app notification, email, or a text if they agreed to texts.
  • One tap on “Not attending today”, with a reason, records the absence and stops the messages.
  • If the child is on the way, no reply is needed: the check closes when they’re signed in.
Text messages use the SMS & voice alerts add-on. Safe Arrival works without it through the app and email.

🧑‍🏫 Your team

  • If the parents haven’t answered by your escalation time, the room’s educators and the centre’s director are alerted.
  • The alert opens the Safe Arrival board, with each guardian’s name and a tap-to-call number.
  • Anyone a phone notification can’t reach gets the alert by email, and the board names them.
  • When a parent reports an absence, the room’s educators and the director are told too.
Staff alerts go out even if a family has turned notifications off: a missing child is the centre’s business.

FAQ

Questions about Safe Arrival

Who gets the first message?

The child’s parents and guardians, once, through the channels each of them chose in their profile: app notification, email, or a text message if they agreed to texts. If they answer “Not attending today”, nothing else is sent.

Who is alerted when the parents don’t answer?

The educators assigned to the child’s room and the centre’s director, in the app and as a phone notification. If no one is attached to that room or centre, the agency’s admins are alerted, so an alert never goes nowhere.

What if an educator’s phone notifications are off?

Anyone the phone notification doesn’t reach gets the same alert by email, and the Safe Arrival board shows their name, so the director can see who wasn’t reached.

Does it run on holidays or days a child doesn’t attend?

No. Only children scheduled for that weekday are checked, and only at a centre that is open that day. Closures and holidays on your calendar are skipped, and a child already reported absent is never asked about.

Do we need the SMS add-on?

No. Safe Arrival is part of KiddieTrac and works with app notifications and email. Text messages to parents use the SMS & voice alerts add-on, and only go to parents who agreed to texts.

Can educators turn it off or change the times?

No. Safe Arrival is off until an agency admin turns it on, and only an agency admin can change its settings. Every change is written to the audit log.

FAQ

Questions about the referral program

How much do I earn?

A one-time $200 CAD for each program you refer that becomes a paying KiddieTrac customer. Refer more than one program, and you earn $200 for each one that joins.

When and how do I get paid?

By e-transfer, once the program you referred has been a paying customer for 60 days. We’ll contact you to arrange it.

What does the program I refer get?

Their first month free: we waive their first monthly subscription fee. Add-ons, such as SMS & voice alerts, are billed as usual.

Who can refer?

Anyone: KiddieTrac customers, educators, consultants, parents, or anyone who knows a childcare program. You can’t refer your own agency or centre.

What if someone else already referred them?

Each new program earns one reward, and the first valid referral we receive gets it. Your referral also has to reach us before the program signs up or books a demo with us another way.

Which programs count?

New customers only. A program that already uses KiddieTrac, or that cancelled in the last 12 months, isn’t eligible.

  1. The reward. KiddieTrac pays the person who refers a program (the referrer) a one-time referral fee of $200 CAD for each eligible program they refer that becomes a paying KiddieTrac customer.

Our Story

Born in Toronto, Built for North America

The Origin Story

KiddieTrac didn't start in a Silicon Valley boardroom. It started from the real frustration of running a childcare agency in Toronto, Ontario — drowning in spreadsheets, manual CWELCC submissions, and billing errors.

We built the software we wished existed. Today, KiddieTrac is used by 150+ agencies across North America — and we're just getting started.

Privacy Policy

Last updated: March 2025 · PIPEDA Compliant

1. Information We Collect

We collect information you provide directly (name, email, agency name, billing information), information generated through use of our platform (attendance records, billing data, communication logs), and technical information (IP address, browser type, device information) for security and analytics purposes.

2. How We Use Your Information

We use your information to provide and improve KiddieTrac services, process payments, send service notifications, comply with legal obligations under PIPEDA and provincial privacy laws, and generate anonymized analytics to improve our platform.

3. Data Storage & Location

All data is stored on servers located in Canada and the United States. We use enterprise-grade encryption (AES-256) at rest and in transit. We do not store data in jurisdictions outside North America.

4. PIPEDA Compliance

KiddieTrac is fully compliant with the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA). You have the right to access, correct, and request deletion of your personal information at any time by contacting us through our contact form.

5. Children's Privacy

We take the privacy of children in our care data extremely seriously. Child profiles and activity data are accessible only to authorized parents and approved staff. We never share children's data with third parties for marketing purposes.

6. Data Retention

We retain your data for the duration of your subscription plus 2 years, after which it is securely deleted. You may request deletion at any time. Backups are purged within 90 days of deletion requests.

7. Third-Party Services

We use carefully vetted third-party services including Stripe (payment processing), an email delivery service, secure North American data centres (infrastructure), and Google Analytics (anonymized usage). All third parties are contractually bound to our privacy standards.

8. Cookies & Analytics

This website uses strictly necessary storage to work: remembering your cookie choice, your language and form security. With your permission it also uses analytics cookies (Google Analytics 4, with IP anonymisation) to understand which pages are useful. Analytics only runs after you choose “Accept all” or switch it on, and turning it off deletes those cookies. We do not use advertising, retargeting or cross-site tracking cookies. You can change your choice at any time: Cookie settings.

9. Contact Us

For privacy inquiries: Contact us

How we protect you

Security at every layer

All data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2+ and encrypted at rest. Sensitive fields, such as two-factor secrets, are additionally encrypted at the application layer.

Your data is hosted in North American data centres and never leaves the continent. If your organization requires data stored in Canada, please talk to us before you sign up.

Automated backups run twice daily with point-in-time recovery, so your records stay safe even in the rare event of an incident.

Two-factor authentication and granular, role-based permissions ensure staff only see what they need. Platform admins, agency admins, directors, educators and guardians each have scoped access.

Your data is always yours. Export to PDF, CSV or Excel anytime, and request deletion in line with our documented data-retention policy.

We monitor the platform around the clock and follow a documented incident-response process, including timely notification where required by law.

Please tell us. Our vulnerability reporting policy explains how to report it, what's in scope, and how we work with researchers.

Vendor Assessment

Questions about security?

Our team is happy to walk through our practices or complete your vendor security assessment.

Security

Vulnerability Reporting

Help us keep children's and families' information safe. If you've found a security issue in KiddieTrac, we want to hear from you.

Security at KiddieTrac

KiddieTrac holds some of the most sensitive information there is: children's records, family contacts, health notes and billing. Protecting it is part of how we build every feature:

  • Encrypted connections (TLS) for the website, the portal and the apps.
  • Two-factor sign-in and passkeys, with role-based access so each person sees only what their role allows.
  • Each agency's data kept separate from every other agency's, with automated checks that look for data crossing between them.
  • An audit log of sensitive actions, and security alerts on suspicious sign-in activity.
  • Automated nightly backups, stored away from the website and checked that they ran.
  • Card payments handled by our payment processors, so KiddieTrac never stores full card numbers.

Shared responsibility

We secure the platform and its code. Agencies and families keep their own accounts safe: use a strong, unique password or a passkey, turn on two-factor sign-in, never share a login, and remove access for staff who leave.

How to report a vulnerability

Email info@kiddietrac.com with the subject line Security report. Please include:

  • What the issue is, and where: the page, screen, URL or API endpoint.
  • Step-by-step instructions to reproduce it, in the body of the email (text, or PNG/JPG screenshots). Please don't send other attachments.
  • What an attacker could do with it, as you understand it.
  • How to reach you, and the name or handle you'd like to be credited with.

If you came across anyone else's personal information, please don't include it in your report. Describe it instead, and delete anything you saved.

What happens next

  • We aim to acknowledge your report within 3 business days.
  • We'll confirm whether we can reproduce it, and keep you updated while we work on a fix.
  • We prioritise by severity and by the risk to families' information. Anything that could expose one agency's or family's data to someone else comes first.
  • We'll tell you when it's fixed and, if you'd like, credit you.

In scope

www.kiddietrac.com, app.kiddietrac.com, api.kiddietrac.com, and the KiddieTrac mobile apps. We're especially interested in:

  • Access to another agency's, family's or person's data (broken access control, IDOR, tenant isolation).
  • Authentication and session flaws: sign-in, password reset, two-factor, passkeys.
  • Cross-site scripting (XSS) and cross-site request forgery (CSRF).
  • SQL injection, server-side request forgery (SSRF), template injection and remote code execution.
  • Exposure of sensitive data, and TLS or HTTPS misconfiguration.

Out of scope

  • Social engineering or phishing of our staff, agencies or families.
  • Physical attacks, and attacks that need access to someone's unlocked device.
  • Denial of service, load or volume testing, and anything that degrades the service for others.
  • Spam or rate-limit findings without a security impact, and self-XSS.
  • Missing best-practice headers or settings with no demonstrated way to exploit them.
  • Issues that need the victim to install unusual software or use an unsupported browser.
  • Bugs in third-party services we use (for example payment, messaging or email providers). Please report those to the provider.
  • Visual and usability bugs. Please tell us through the contact page instead.

Testing in good faith

  • Use only accounts you own or that we've given you for testing. Never another person's account.
  • If you reach someone else's information, stop there, don't view, change or keep more than you need to show the problem, and report it straight away.
  • Don't run automated scanners at a volume that affects the service, and don't send messages, texts or calls to real families.
  • Give us a reasonable time to fix the issue before you share it with anyone else.

If you act in good faith and follow this policy, we'll treat your research as authorised, work with you to understand and fix the issue, and won't pursue legal action against you for it.

Recognition

We're grateful to everyone who helps keep KiddieTrac safe. With your permission, we'll thank you by name or handle once the issue is fixed. We don't offer monetary rewards.

🔒 Questions about our security practices, or a vendor security assessment? See Security & Trust or contact our team.
Accessibility

Accessibility Policy

Childcare runs on everyone being able to take part — families, educators and our own team. We're committed to removing barriers wherever we find them.

Last updated: September 29, 2026

Our commitment

KiddieTrac is committed to treating everyone with dignity and independence, and to giving people with disabilities the same opportunity to use our products and services, and to work with us, as everyone else. We meet our obligations under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 (AODA), its Integrated Accessibility Standards, and the Ontario Human Rights Code, and we work to identify, remove and prevent barriers.

Accessible by design: our website, portal and apps

We design KiddieTrac to work for as many people as possible and use the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, Level AA as our standard for the website, the portal and the mobile apps. We are reviewing our screens against it and fixing what we find. Today:

  • The portal is available in English, French, Spanish and Hindi, and our website in English, French and Spanish.
  • Families can choose how they hear from their centre — in the app, by email, by text, or by an automated phone call for urgent notices — so important information doesn't depend on one way of reading it.
  • The portal works in a web browser, on phones and tablets, and in our mobile apps, so people can use the device and assistive tools they already rely on.
  • Parts of the portal respect your device's "reduce motion" setting.

If any part of KiddieTrac is hard to use with your assistive technology, please tell us. We'll help you get the information or complete the task another way while we fix it.

Customer service

  • Assistive devices: people may use their own assistive devices to access our services.
  • Support persons: a person with a disability may be accompanied by a support person in any meeting, training or demonstration.
  • Service animals: service animals are welcome anywhere we meet with customers in person.
  • Communication: we communicate in a way that takes a person's disability into account — for example by email instead of phone, with more time, or in plain language.
  • Service disruptions: if a planned or unplanned disruption affects the service, we post notice in the portal and by email, with the reason, how long it's expected to last, and any alternatives.

Information and communications

On request, we provide our public information — including this policy, our guides and emergency or safety information — in an accessible format or with communication supports, in a timely manner and at no extra cost. We'll work with you to find a suitable format. If something truly can't be converted, we'll explain why and give you a summary.

Employment

  • We tell applicants that accommodations are available throughout recruitment, from applying to interviews and assessments, and to new hires as part of onboarding.
  • We work with employees who have disabilities on individual accommodation plans, and with those who need it on individualized workplace emergency response information.
  • We take accessibility needs into account in performance management, career development and return-to-work.
  • Workplace information is available in accessible formats on request.

Training

Everyone who works for or on behalf of KiddieTrac receives training on the AODA's Integrated Accessibility Standards and the Ontario Human Rights Code as it relates to people with disabilities — including how to communicate with people with different disabilities and how to help someone using an assistive device, a service animal or a support person. New team members are trained as part of onboarding, and training is refreshed when our policies change.

Feedback

We welcome feedback about how we provide accessible products and services. Email info@kiddietrac.com with the subject Accessibility, or use our contact form. Feedback can also be given in another format on request. We aim to acknowledge feedback within 5 business days and to tell you what we'll do about it.

Changes to this policy

We review this policy regularly and whenever our products or obligations change. Any policy that doesn't respect and promote the dignity and independence of people with disabilities will be modified or removed.

Our values

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Policy

Every child deserves to be seen, and every family to feel welcome. We hold ourselves, and what we build, to the same standard.

Last updated: September 29, 2026

Why it matters to us

KiddieTrac serves childcare providers and the families who trust them — families of every background, culture, language, faith, ability and shape. We believe a diverse team builds better software for them, and that an equitable, inclusive workplace is simply the right way to work.

Scope

This policy applies to everyone who works for or with KiddieTrac — employees, contractors and applicants — and to how we treat our customers, partners and the families who use our products.

Equal opportunity and non-discrimination

We do not discriminate on any ground protected by the Ontario Human Rights Code or other applicable law, including race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or family status, and disability. Hiring, pay, promotion, training and every other employment decision is based on the requirements of the job and a person's qualifications, skills and contribution.

Inclusive hiring

  • Job postings describe what the role truly requires and invite applicants to request accommodations.
  • Candidates for a role are assessed against the same criteria, by more than one person where possible.
  • We look beyond our immediate networks when we recruit, so that more people hear about our opportunities.

A respectful, inclusive workplace

  • We don't tolerate harassment, discrimination or bullying of any kind, and we act on every concern raised.
  • We provide accommodation to the point of undue hardship, including for disability, religious observance and family status (see our Accessibility Policy).
  • We respect the names and pronouns people use, and we build flexibility into how and when work gets done where the role allows.
  • Everyone is expected to contribute to an environment where people can speak up, disagree respectfully and do their best work.

Inclusive by design: our product

  • The portal is available in several languages — English, French, Spanish and Hindi — so families and educators can use it in the language they're most comfortable with.
  • Children's records include pronouns and preferred names, and cultural and dietary notes, so educators can care for each child as the family asks.
  • Families are made of guardians of every kind: our records let a family name each guardian and their relationship to the child, rather than assuming two parents.
  • Families choose how they hear from their centre — app, email, text or phone — so information reaches everyone.
  • We consider the needs of diverse families and educators when we design new features, and we welcome feedback when we get something wrong.

Raising a concern

Anyone who experiences or sees behaviour that goes against this policy is encouraged to raise it with their manager or by emailing info@kiddietrac.com. Concerns are handled promptly, fairly and as confidentially as possible. We do not tolerate retaliation against anyone who raises a concern in good faith.

Accountability

KiddieTrac's leadership is responsible for this policy. We review it at least once a year, alongside our hiring and workplace practices, and update it as we learn.

Internet Safety

Staying safe online, together

Families trust childcare with the people they love most, and with a lot of personal information. Here's how KiddieTrac helps keep it safe, and simple steps everyone can take.

Why it matters

A childcare account holds names, photos, addresses, health notes and payment details. That makes it worth protecting carefully. Most online harm doesn't come from sophisticated attacks: it comes from a reused password, a convincing fake email, or a photo shared further than intended. A few good habits go a long way.

How KiddieTrac protects your information

🔐 Secure sign-in

  • Two-factor authentication, and passkeys that sign you in with your face, fingerprint or device PIN.
  • New accounts start with a one-time temporary password that must be changed at first sign-in.
  • All traffic between your device and KiddieTrac is encrypted.

👥 The right people, and only them

  • Everyone sees only what their role needs: guardians see their own family, educators their own rooms.
  • Each agency's records are kept separate from every other agency's.
  • Sensitive actions are recorded in an audit log.

📸 Your photos stay yours

  • Photos and videos are shared with families inside the app, not on public pages or social media.
  • Your information is used to run your childcare service, as our Privacy Policy explains, and our site uses no advertising or tracking cookies.

🛡️ Behind the scenes

  • Regular backups, security monitoring and a documented incident process.
  • Read the details on our Security & Trust page.
KiddieTrac will never ask for your password — not by email, text message or phone call, and not even when you contact our support team. If anyone asks, it isn't us. Please don't share it, and let us know.

Tips for parents and guardians

  • Use a strong, unique password. At least 12 characters, not used on any other site. A passphrase of a few unrelated words is easy to remember and hard to guess. Better still, turn on a passkey or two-factor sign-in.
  • Check before you click. KiddieTrac emails come from kiddietrac.com or from your own childcare provider. If a message feels urgent, unusual or asks you to pay somewhere new, open the app directly instead of using the link.
  • Share photos thoughtfully. Photos from your centre often include other children. Please keep them private, and ask before posting anything that shows someone else's child.
  • Keep your details current. Up-to-date phone numbers, emergency contacts and pickup permissions help your centre reach the right people quickly.
  • Sign out on shared devices, and keep your phone's software up to date.

Tips for educators and directors

  • Never share a login. Every team member should have their own account, so access matches their role and the record shows who did what.
  • Use the app for family photos and messages rather than personal phones, texts or social media.
  • Lock your device when you step away, and remove access promptly when someone leaves your team.
  • Be wary of unexpected requests to change a family's payment details or contact information; confirm them in person or by a known phone number.

Talking with children about the internet

Online safety starts early. Keep screens in shared spaces, explore together, and let children know they can always tell a trusted adult if something online makes them feel worried or uncomfortable — and that they won't be in trouble for telling.

Seen something suspicious?

If you receive a message that claims to be from KiddieTrac but doesn't feel right, or you think someone else has accessed your account, contact us right away at info@kiddietrac.com or 1-855-400-9996, and change your password. For concerns about your child's own records, you can also speak with your childcare provider.

What's New

Product updates & releases

We ship improvements every week. Here's what's landed recently.

October 2026 NEW

🍁 Built for Ontario’s rules

For Ontario centres and agencies: live ratio checks against O. Reg. 137/15, sleep room checks, OCCMS fee subsidy reporting and ECE workforce funding in payroll, plus tools for the January 2027 changes: name-to-face headcounts with an acting supervisor, missing-child drills, a hazard register and policy sign-offs with a training matrix. See what’s built for Ontario

October 2026 NEW

🛡️ Safe Arrival

When a child expected today hasn’t been signed in and no absence was reported, KiddieTrac asks the parents, then alerts the room’s educators and the director if nobody answers. Anyone a phone notification can’t reach gets the alert by email. A live board shows who still needs a call, and every check is recorded. See Safe Arrival

October 2026 NEW

📘 Sage Accounting sync & Sage 50 export

Connect Sage Accounting and invoices, voids and payments sync just like Xero and QuickBooks. On Sage 50 desktop? Download a balanced general journal file and a customers file to import. Each file holds only what is new since the last one.

October 2026 NEW

📗 Xero sync

Connect your own Xero app and send invoices, voids and payments straight to your Xero organisation. Families become Xero contacts, invoices keep their KiddieTrac numbers, and syncing again updates them instead of making copies.

September 2026 NEW

💳 Card payments with Helcim

A third payment provider alongside Zūm Rails and Stripe. Cards are collected inside Helcim's own secure checkout, so card numbers never reach KiddieTrac, and each payment is confirmed server-side before it counts against an invoice.

September 2026 NEW

📞 Voice announcement calls & Telnyx SMS

Broadcast an urgent announcement as an automated phone call, not just a text. SMS can now run on Telnyx as well as Twilio, with automatic failover if a carrier is unavailable.

September 2026 NEW

✅ Text-alert consent records

Every opt-in and opt-out is confirmed to the family by email and text and filed in their documents. A STOP reply now applies to every account tied to that phone number.

September 2026 NEW

🗓️ Payment schedules & service fees

Instalment plans issue each invoice a set number of days before it is due. Agencies can optionally apply card and EFT service-fee percentages at the moment of payment.

September 2026 NEW

🛡️ Verified nightly backups

Every night the platform is backed up and verified, with 14 days retained and a schedule platform admins can adjust.

August 2026 NEW

✉️ Email from your own domain

Invoices, reports and notices can go out from your agency's own Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace mailbox instead of a KiddieTrac address.

August 2026 NEW

🔐 Two-factor sign-in & security alerts

Two-factor authentication for staff accounts, and real-time alerts when something suspicious happens, such as repeated failed sign-ins.

July 2026 NEW

🏡 Home Visitor role

A dedicated role for home-visiting practitioners. Home visitors are added to your agency and log structured home-visit reports — visit type, who was present, summary, strengths, concerns, next steps and a follow-up date — for any centre in the agency, chosen from a simple dropdown. They get the same guided account onboarding as your other team members, and directors and agency admins can review every report in one place. Ideal for early-years home-visiting, family-support and outreach programs.

Parent-ready daily summaries generated automatically from the day's activities, meals and notes — saving educators time and delighting families.
